capabilities.description: Replaces `_line_in_region`'s single fixed-padding touch boolean with a richer relation (LineRegionRelation: intersection ratios, center/baseline containment, overflow per edge, genuine overlap against the region's own raw pre-growth extent, and a match against growth's own authoritative absorbed-label record) and a per-consumer policy (_text_consumption_decision: text removal from the rendered Markdown requires containment, genuine raw-extent overlap, or a matched absorption - never mere touching or partial overlap, and an inconclusive relation is treated as 'ambiguous', which always keeps the line visible rather than risking silent deletion). Closes a whole neighboring column's own unrelated body text (or a real statement's own opening/closing lines) being silently dropped just because a region's *grown* bbox brushes its edge by a few points. `raw_intersects` requires clearing REGION_Y_PADDING (2.0pt, the same noise floor used elsewhere) on both axes, not a bare >0 check - found necessary when a noise-level ~1.6pt raw-bbox graze against a *different*, neighboring region's raw extent (2008-b D40's own SQL schema line) was otherwise treated as decisive evidence.
trigger_features: a text line's own bbox tested for genuine overlap/containment against a region's grown bbox, its raw (pre-growth) bbox, and its own growth-absorbed label list - three independent geometric signals, none of them a single fixed threshold
capabilities.scope: assembler.py: LineRegionRelation / compute_line_region_relation / _text_consumption_decision / _line_in_region; figures.py: VisualRegion.raw_bbox / VisualRegion.absorbed_label_bboxes (populated by _expand_with_labels' own optional absorbed_out parameter)

Q02/Q12/Q45/Q54/Q63/Q71/Q75 (own real statement text partially-to-substantially recovered; Q75's own statement now fully complete)

Q24 (garbled diagram-label fragments removed, though the question's own separate merged-region defect remains)
D40 (Cliente(...) schema code line's own first printed line restored after a brief in-phase regression from the pre-REGION_Y_PADDING-floor version of raw_intersects)

capabilities.failure_behavior: False (original fixed-padding behavior, byte-identical) when the profile does not set this field; an inconclusive relation (state other than 'contained', no raw overlap, no absorbed-label match, not a small-formula region) is always 'ambiguous' -> the line stays visible, never silently removed. Two known, documented trade-offs of this fail-safe-visible design (see docs/phase-3g-report.md): Q07 loses one additional already-fragmented word ('aos') that growth's own pre-existing over-absorption chain genuinely records as absorbed (same family as geometric_word_fragment_reconstruction's own open cases); D40's own query-tree 'F' label, previously swallowed by the old unconditional touch tolerance, now leaks as visible text rather than being silently (and here, correctly) hidden, since it is geometrically indistinguishable from the touching-only false positives this mechanism exists to reject.

capabilities.description: Narrows `_line_in_region`'s own blanket exemption for any alternative-marker-shaped line ("A\t...") to require that it also sit at the page's own established body-text margin (figures._is_marker_at_margin, with a text-length-based fallback margin - dominant_left_margin_by_text_length - for a page whose real body column is itself too narrow for the width-based margin to find enough evidence) before protecting it from region membership outright. A marker-shaped line that is NOT at that margin (a diagram-internal label - an automaton input, an ER-diagram entity name, a grammar-production metavariable) falls through to the same contextual_line_region_relation as any other line, and is correctly hidden when it is genuinely part of the diagram. This is a narrower, more surgical mechanism than the full alternative_group confidence-scored structure the Phase 3G prompt describes (candidate_labels/expected_sequence/alignment/font_features/spacing_pattern/column/competing_group/confidence) - it achieves the same practical outcome for every real case found this phase (Q24/Q29/Q63) via one relative geometric signal already validated elsewhere in this codebase, rather than a new, larger-surface structure; the fuller alternative_group architecture remains a documented future improvement, not yet needed.
trigger_features: a line matching the alternative/question marker text shape (_ALTERNATIVE_MARKER_RE/_QUESTION_MARKER_RE) AND its own x0 within _MARGIN_TOLERANCE of the page's own dominant left margin (width-based, or text-length-based when width-based finds no confident margin)

parameters.contextual_relation_gate: bool, default False (shares the gate with contextual_line_region_relation - both are part of the same Phase 3G _line_in_region replacement)

capabilities.scope: assembler.py: _line_in_region (marker check), reusing figures._is_marker_at_margin; figures.py: dominant_left_margin_by_text_length (extracted from _dominant_body_font_size)
real_cases: 2008-b Q29 (page 13, grammar-production 'A -> a'/'B -> b' fully resolved), Q63 (page 27, ER-diagram entity names 'A'/'B'/'C' no longer leak), Q24 (page 12, decoder input labels 'A'/'B' no longer leak, though the question's own separate merged-region defect remains)

capabilities.description: IMPLEMENTED IN PHASE 3H ("Cluster D"). Rejoins a physical line PyMuPDF's own get_text("dict") reported as several separate same-baseline "line" entries, using two documentary signals together (never a dictionary or language model): a literal trailing space in the earlier fragment's own raw glyph stream, and a horizontal gap within a font-size-relative safety ceiling (real fragmentation gaps measured at ~0.84-0.92x the shared font size; real table-cell gaps at ~2.5-4.1x - an order-of-magnitude-class separation). A detected column boundary (the same detect_column_margins already used for reading order) is never crossed, closing a real false positive found against the protected 2021 corpus (two independent, side-by-side objective questions whose own first lines happen to share a baseline). A companion fix in figures.py excludes any fragment-merged line from label_candidates outright, regardless of width - a genuinely fragmented-and-reconstructed line is, by construction, continuous body/alternative prose, never an atomic diagram label; without this, a reconstructed line narrow enough to look like a label by coincidence was absorbed as one unit the moment any part of it touched a growing region's own bbox (found against 2008-b Q07: worse than the pre-merge fragments, which only an unlucky subset of could ever individually reach).
trigger_features: two or more raw PyMuPDF dict-mode line entries on the same page sharing an (almost) identical baseline (y0 and y1 within 0.05pt), both non-monospace, compatible font size (within 0.5pt), separated by a positive horizontal gap within MAX_FRAGMENT_GAP_RATIO (1.5x the shared font size), with the earlier fragment's own raw (pre-normalization) text ending in a literal space character - AND not straddling this page's own detected column boundary
capabilities.scope: layout.py: _raw_lines/_collect_raw_fragments/_build_line_from_group/_column_boundary_for_fragment_merge/Line.fragment_merges; fragment_reconstruction.py: RawLineFragment/LineFragmentRelation/compute_line_fragment_relation/group_line_fragments/FragmentMergeTrace (new module); figures.py: label_candidates excludes any line with non-empty fragment_merges

Q12 (page 8, 'base na complexidade ciclomatica.' rejoined - statement now 100% complete, question flips to passed)
Q63 (page 27, 'a seguinte representacao de' rejoined - statement now 100% complete, question flips to passed)

capabilities.failure_behavior: False (original per-dict-line behavior, byte-identical) when the profile does not set this field. When ambiguous (baseline matches but no trailing space, or a trailing space but the gap exceeds the ceiling, or a detected column boundary is crossed), fragments are preserved exactly as PyMuPDF reported them - never destructively joined on a guess. Confirmed by full regeneration that this mechanism DOES fix an unrelated, already-documented 2021 defect (layout.py's own 'B Escalonamento por taxas monotonicas' MIN_LINES_PER_COLUMN docstring) when tried unconditionally - gated regardless, since any protected-corpus change is reverted on principle, not only when it is wrong.

capabilities.description: Replaces the old assembler._find_alternative_starts (an isolated, right-to-left, margin-unaware search for the last capital letter A..E it could find) with a structural evaluation of the whole A-E label sequence as one group (alternative_groups.find_alternative_group). Collects every line matching the marker shape into per-letter AlternativeMarkerCandidate pools, computes a reference_margin (the mode of every candidate's own x0, trusted only when backed by at least _MIN_MARGIN_VOTES=2 real votes), then resolves each letter from E back to A: a letter with a single candidate is trivially accepted; a letter with multiple candidates is narrowed to its on-margin subset only when that subset is a strict, non-empty partition of its own candidates (never all-or-nothing), and the pre-existing last-candidate-before-the-next-letter reading-order rule is always the final tie-break within whichever pool applies. Margin evidence is a refinement layered on top of reading order, never a replacement for it - ordinary body prose beginning with a bare capital letter routinely shares the same left margin as a real marker in this corpus, so margin alone cannot discriminate.
trigger_features: a line's own text exactly matches ^([A-E])(?:[\t ](.*))?$ (the same shape assembler.py's own alternative-line regex expects)
capabilities.scope: alternative_groups.py: find_alternative_group / _reference_margin; assembler.py: both call sites that previously called _find_alternative_starts (function removed)
real_cases: 2008-b Q71 (alternative B/C cross-contamination fully resolved - the phase's own obligatory case)
2008-b Q28 (page 13, horizontal grid layout; a body-prose false 'A' sharing the real marker's own margin correctly loses to the real marker via reading order)
2008-b Q52 (page 22, same shape as Q28)
protected_cases: 2011 Q39 (page 25, a fully horizontal, no-shared-margin alternative layout with a judged-item's own false 'A' candidate coincidentally sharing no margin with anything - required _MIN_MARGIN_VOTES to avoid a real regression; confirmed fixed and non-regressing afterwards)
every other 2011/2021 question (zero byte-level drift confirmed via SHA-256 baseline across every fix iteration this phase)
capabilities.failure_behavior: returns None (assembler.py falls back to its own pre-existing generic 'nao foi possivel localizar' warning path, exactly as the old function's own None return did) when letter E has zero candidates; returns a group with status='incomplete' (also treated as unusable via AlternativeGroup.is_usable) when some other letter has zero candidates before the next accepted letter's own line - never fabricates a boundary, never consults the gabarito
capabilities.profile_dependency: none - unconditional replacement of _find_alternative_starts for every corpus, not gated by ExamStructureProfile, because two full regression rounds (the Q28/Q52 re-check, then the 2011 Q39 re-check) confirmed it strictly improves on the old algorithm with zero drift elsewhere once _MIN_MARGIN_VOTES was added, so no backward-compatible opt-out was needed

capabilities.description: Covers the complementary, boundary-selection half of distinguishing a real alternative marker from a diagram-internal or body-prose line that merely shares the same 'single capital letter A-E' text shape - the region-membership half (whether such a line is hidden from a visual region's own bounding box) is the pre-existing diagram_internal_label_margin_check (Phase 3G); this capability is what determines which competing marker-shaped candidate actually anchors an alternative's own start line, inside alternative_groups.find_alternative_group. A false candidate is rejected not by classifying its text semantically (e.g. never by detecting 'this looks like an automaton input label') but purely structurally: it either falls outside the reference_margin's own on-margin subset when that subset is a genuine, non-empty partition of the letter's own candidates, or it loses the final reading-order tie-break to a later, genuine marker on the same margin. No positive catalogue of diagram-label shapes is maintained or matched against.
trigger_features: two or more candidates for the same letter within one question's own alt_section span, where at least one is not the genuine alternative marker
real_cases: 2008-b Q71 (a false 'C'/'B'-shaped line inside the alternatives' own wrapped prose no longer wins over the genuine marker)
2008-b Q28/Q52 (a body-prose sentence beginning with a bare 'A' sharing the real marker's own left margin no longer wins the boundary)
protected_cases: 2011 Q39 (the judged-item false 'A' candidate that motivated _MIN_MARGIN_VOTES)
every real alternative marker in 2011/2021/2008-b (the genuine marker is never rejected by this mechanism in any of the 65 currently-passing 2008-b questions or any 2011/2021 question)
capabilities.failure_behavior: when no structural signal (margin partition, then reading order) can separate two candidates for the same letter, the later candidate always wins deterministically (last-wins reading order) rather than the group being marked ambiguous - real-corpus evidence this phase never actually produced a genuine, structurally-tied case, so an ambiguous outcome remains architecturally supported (AlternativeGroupStatus) but is not currently reachable by any implemented rule; see docs/phase-3i-report.md
capabilities.profile_dependency: none - shares alternative_group's own unconditional scope

capabilities.description: Once find_alternative_group returns a resolved, usable group, assembler.py slices a question's own text_only_lines into each alternative's own line range directly from AlternativeGroup.accepted (a {letter: line_index} map), in place of the old function's own returned start-index list; the downstream cutoff/statement/table-slicing logic is otherwise unchanged (same code, only the source of each per-letter start index changed). This is the mechanism that actually places Q71's own B/C boundary on the correct line instead of leaking the tail of one alternative's own content into its neighbor.
trigger_features: an alt_section span whose lines produce a resolved, usable AlternativeGroup
capabilities.scope: assembler.py (main alternative-assembly call site and the preliminary alt-section-start detection call site)
real_cases: 2008-b Q71 (page ~37-38, alternatives B and C - the phase's own obligatory case, verified via exact string equality against the real PDF source text)
protected_cases: every other question whose alternatives were already correctly bounded before this phase (Q07/Q12/Q13/Q25/Q29/Q61/Q62/Q63/Q68/Q75, 2011 Q34, all confirmed non-regressed)
capabilities.failure_behavior: an unusable AlternativeGroup (None or status != 'resolved') leaves the question's own alternative section unassembled and emits a warning, exactly as the old function's own failure path did - never a partial or guessed boundary
capabilities.profile_dependency: none - shares alternative_group's own unconditional scope

capabilities.description: Guarantees that a question's own statement slice and every one of its own alternative slices are computed from the *same* reading-order-preserving line list and can never overlap by construction - the general, single-source-ownership principle behind the Q13 fix (PROMPT Phase 3J). Before this phase, assembler.assemble_question computed the statement's own cutoff via a geometric (page, y0) comparison (assembler._position_key) used as a *proxy* for 'before the first alternative in reading order' - correct whenever a line's own y0 and its own reading-order position happen to move together, but silently wrong for a line that is genuinely last in reading order yet has a smaller raw y0 (a column-overflow line, printed at the top of the next column because it did not fit at the bottom of its own). assembler._reading_order_index instead locates the exact reading-order position of the alternative-group's own cutoff line within content_lines and slices there directly, so the statement can never re-admit a line that the alternative group already correctly claimed, for any question, not only Q13's own shape.
trigger_features: n/a - runs unconditionally for every objective question with a resolved alternative group, not triggered by a document characteristic
negative_fixtures: the Section 20 corpus-wide scan (docs/phase-3j-report.md) confirms zero line-identity duplicate-destination findings across all 77 published 2008-b questions after this fix
real_cases: 2008-b Q13 (page 8, alternative E's own column-overflow line was published in both the statement and alternative E at once)
protected_cases: every other 2008-b/2011/2021 question (zero byte-level drift confirmed via SHA-256 baseline)
capabilities.failure_behavior: an unresolved or unusable alternative group leaves the statement as the full content_lines, exactly as before this phase - never a partial or guessed cutoff
capabilities.profile_dependency: none - unconditional replacement of the old position-key cutoff for every corpus

capabilities.description: Reattaches a document annotation (currently: only '(valor: X pontos)' scoring annotations - see question_value_annotation below) to the item it structurally belongs to, by real geometric interval containment against each item's own printed position - never by reading-order adjacency and never by the annotation's own text content beyond confirming it matches the annotation's own shape. Owner (which item), anchor (the item's own real position) and destination (where the annotation ends up in the rebuilt line list) are three separate concerns (PROMPT Phase 3J section 7): proximity to a neighboring line in the buggy reading order is never treated as evidence of ownership.
trigger_features: at least one line in a question's own span matches the annotation shape (see question_value_annotation) AND at least one lettered item marker (A-E) is present in the same span
real_cases: 2008-b D60 (page 26, three per-item annotations bunched at the end of the reading order, item C published with item A's own value)
protected_cases: 2008-b D80 (page 35, two per-item annotations already correctly interleaved - confirmed a true content no-op)
2008-b D9/D10/D20/D39/D40/D59/D79 (every fused-inline annotation, never matched by the whole-line regex at all)
every 2011/2021 discursive question with a '(valor:' annotation (zero drift)
capabilities.failure_behavior: no item markers found at all leaves every annotation exactly where it was (status left as a single overall value, not per-item) - never guesses an owner
capabilities.profile_dependency: none - unconditional, gated only by the presence of the annotation shape itself

capabilities.description: The concrete annotation type this phase has real evidence for: a parenthesized '(valor: X pontos)' scoring annotation (decimal separator, singular/plural and whitespace all vary across the corpus but the shape is otherwise fixed). A narrower, evidenced instance of the broader DocumentAnnotation/AnnotationType architecture (annotations.py) - the other declared types (instruction, figure_reference, table_reference, source_citation, answer_area_label, section_note, chrome, ambiguous) have no detection logic implemented, since no real positive and negative corpus case for any of them was found this phase (see docs/generalization-contract.md section 1.1).

protected_cases: 2008-b D80, D9/D10/D20/D39/D40/D59/D79; every 2011/2021 discursive question with a value annotation
capabilities.failure_behavior: a line that does not match the whole-line pattern is never treated as an annotation, even if it contains the word 'valor' as part of a longer sentence

capabilities.description: A standalone, read-only audit (never wired into the live extraction pipeline) that flags a source element published to more than one destination, owner, or alternative - grouped strictly by source_element_id (real, stable PDF geometry), never by text equality, so two alternatives that legitimately share identical wording are never flagged (PROMPT Phase 3J section 9). Runs against the content-assignment ledger (scripts/generate_content_assignment_ledger.py, data/manifests/content-assignment-2008-b.json) generated by re-running the real pipeline with a read-only instrumentation hook. Reports only - a gate can never decide which of two competing destinations is documentally correct; that judgment belongs to the general mechanism that produced the assignment in the first place (canonical_content_assignment/annotation_ownership above), not to a post-hoc gate.
trigger_features: n/a - runs unconditionally over every record in a given content-assignment ledger, not triggered by a document characteristic
real_cases: run against the full 2008-b content-assignment ledger (2280 records, 77 questions): zero duplicate findings, zero missing-assignment findings, after the Q13/D60 fixes
protected_cases: the ledger itself only ever covers 2008-b (generated by re-running its own extraction with a temp output directory) - never touches 2011/2021's own published files
capabilities.failure_behavior: an empty findings list means 'checked, none found' - the gate never silently skips a record
capabilities.profile_dependency: none - invoked as a standalone script/audit, not automatically as part of extract_exam

capabilities.description: Replaces layout.extract_page_lines's own single, page-wide (left_margin, right_margin) column split with a zone-aware resolution (reading_zones.py) for a page whose column topology changes partway down - a photo-and-article zone, then full-width prose, then a two-column bulleted list, all on the same page (2008-b's own D10, 'Formacao Geral Discursiva 10'). layout.detect_column_margins keeps its existing job unchanged (page-wide evidence for whether a genuine two-column shape exists at all, and its two candidate margins); reading_zones answers a separate question - which specific vertical windows of the page actually exhibit both columns concurrently (real, substantial evidence on both sides, genuinely overlapping in Y - never merely because some line's own x0 sits past the page-wide right margin) and therefore need left-then-right interleaving there, versus windows with only one side's real content, which need nothing more than being merged, by y0, into the surrounding flow. The final order is built and verified as a small dependency graph (one node per line, edges tagged with why: same_column_vertical / cross_column_transition / spanning_barrier) and resolved with graphlib.TopologicalSorter - a real cycle raises CycleError and reverts to plain document order rather than ever being silently broken.
trigger_features: a page carries a documented, hash-locked force_zoned_reading_order_page override in data/manifests/layout-overrides.yaml (matched by pdf_sha256 + page number) - never a document characteristic detected automatically

parameters.zoned_reading_order_gate: bool, default False (ExamStructureProfile) - declares the mechanism available for a booklet, does not by itself activate it on any page
parameters.force_zoned_reading_order_page: layout override rule kind (pdf_sha256 + page) - the actual per-page activation switch

capabilities.scope: layout.py: extract_page_lines (consumes both gates together); layout_overrides.py: LayoutOverrideSet.forces_zoned_reading_order; reading_zones.py: detect_reading_zones, resolve_reading_order, zoned_reading_order (new module)
real_cases: 2008-b D10 (page 7): three topology changes on one page - photo+article (two-column), full-width motivating prose, two-column bulleted 'Observacoes' box - all resolved to the correct sequence, confirmed by a full word-set comparison against the raw PDF text (478 words each side, zero missing, zero added)
protected_cases: every other 2008-b page with genuine column evidence (Q28, Q29, Q52, Q61, Q62, Q63, Q68, Q71 among many others) - confirmed unaffected only because activation is page-scoped: an earlier, booklet-wide-gate-only attempt (no page override requirement) regressed dozens of these, since extract_page_lines's own output order feeds other order-dependent heuristics elsewhere in the pipeline (figures.py's own label-absorption _is_paragraph_continuation chief among them) tuned against the old, page-wide split; reverted in favor of requiring both the profile gate and a documented per-page override
every 2011/2021 page (zero byte-level drift confirmed via SHA-256 baseline) - neither profile sets zoned_reading_order_gate at all
capabilities.failure_behavior: a page with no page-wide column evidence at all (detect_column_margins returns None) resolves to one single_column zone sorted by (y0, x0), identical to the pre-existing fallback; a genuine graph cycle (not reached by any real case this phase found - the construction is a linear chain by design) reverts to plain document order and records the cycle in the trace rather than guessing an order or dropping content
capabilities.profile_dependency: ExamStructureProfile.zoned_reading_order_gate (default False) AND a page-specific data/manifests/layout-overrides.yaml entry (rule: force_zoned_reading_order_page) - both required together; the profile field alone never activates the mechanism on any page
